questiontext: Express \[{{CT:0}}\] as a sum of a linear function and a rational function with a linear numerator and denominator {{CT:1}}. [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: We note that the numerator {{CT:2}} is cubic and that the denominator {{CT:1}} is quadratic. Dividing {{CT:2}} by {{CT:1}} we obtain a quotient with a linear numerator of the form {{CT:3}} and a linear term of the form {{CT:4}}, that is \[{{CT:0}}=\frac{{CT:5}}{{CT:6}}+{{CT:7}}.\] Multiplying through by {{CT:1}} \[{{CT:8}} = ({{CT:6}})({{CT:7}})+{{CT:5}}.\] Expanding out the brackets we find \[{{CT:8}} = {{CT:9}}+{{CT:5}}.\] Matching coefficients in \(x^3\) we see \(m={{CT:10}}\). Matching coefficients in lower order terms and substituting we find that \(n={{CT:11}}\), \(g={{CT:12}}\) and \(h={{CT:13}}\). Therefore \[{{CT:0}}={{CT:14}}.\]
